decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with left arm, lifting and orienting before aligning to the differently oriented mallet. Right arm stays clear.
Advance above the handle while gradually yawing the down-facing grasp to align with its left-to-right shaft. Maintain elbow-up continuity.
Continue the smooth elevated approach and shaft alignment; stay above the mallet until orientation is complete.
Finish down-facing alignment to the shaft and move above its handle end. Descend only partway pending wrist confirmation.
Use wrist view to center the handle between the fingers, refine shaft yaw, and lower toward grasp height.
Make the final small wrist-based alignment and close around the handle near its end; retention will be checked by lifting.
Correct the rejected tensor; lift vertically with the left gripper closed to check mallet retention. No earlier lift was executed.
Mallet shaft remains between the closed fingers. Carry it upward and toward the leftmost key, keeping the left wrist left of center and the right arm stationary.
Carry the retained mallet above the red, leftmost key. Keep its tip elevated while finishing horizontal alignment.
The forward approach reached a continuity guard. Replan from the executed pose: retract the wrist and yaw the elevated mallet forward, improving reach without crossing arms.
Align over the front portion of the leftmost red key, then lower vertically for the first strike. Keep the grip closed and inspect contact before moving right.
The tip appears slightly left and above the red key. Center it a little right, then complete a shallow controlled descent onto that same first key.
Finish the red-key contact, lift the mallet 5 cm clear, then move one key right toward the orange key while elevated.
Lower vertically onto the second, orange key after the preceding 5 cm lift. Keep the mallet firmly retained and do not sweep across keys at contact height.
Lift 5 cm after the orange-key contact and move one key right, aligning above the yellow key without touching intervening surfaces.
Strike the third, yellow key with a vertical descent, keeping the closed grip and fixed horizontal alignment.
Lift 5 cm after the yellow-key contact, then translate above the fourth, green key. Keep the wrist in the left workspace.
Descend vertically to strike the fourth, green key following the clear lift from yellow; maintain the closed grasp.
Lift 5 cm clear of the green key, then move above the fifth, light-blue key in the left-to-right sequence.
Strike the fifth, light-blue key with a vertical descent after the preceding 5 cm lift. Keep the shaft retained and horizontal alignment fixed.
Lift 5 cm after the light-blue-key contact, then move above the sixth, dark-blue key while keeping the tip clear.
Descend vertically to strike the sixth, dark-blue key after the clear lift from light blue. Maintain the closed grasp and fixed horizontal alignment.
Lift the mallet 5 cm after the sixth key, then translate above the seventh, purple key. Keep both arms separated and the left grasp closed.
Strike the seventh, purple key by descending vertically after the preceding 5 cm lift. Keep the mallet retained and horizontal alignment fixed.
Lift 5 cm after the purple-key strike, then align above the eighth and final magenta key. Keep the left wrist left of center and the right arm clear.
Descend vertically to strike the final magenta key, following the clear lift from purple. Keep the grasp closed and horizontal alignment fixed.
Lift the mallet vertically 7 cm after the final magenta-key contact, exceeding the required post-hit clearance. Maintain the closed grasp.
The episode remains active and contacts near the front pegs are uncertain. Return above the keys with clearance and angle the mallet toward their centers for a more definite full sequence.
Continue the elevated return to the red key, angling the retained mallet toward the bar center and away from its front peg.
Lower onto the middle of the leftmost red bar for a more definite first contact, away from the front edge and peg. Inspect before advancing.
Complete the central red-bar contact, lift 5.6 cm, then move above the orange bar without sweeping at contact height.
Refine the elevated tip slightly right toward the orange-bar center, then lower vertically for the second central strike.
Lift 5.5 cm after the central orange-bar strike, then move above the yellow bar while keeping the mallet clear and retained.
Descend vertically onto the center of the third, yellow bar after the clear lift from orange. Keep the mallet retained and horizontal position fixed.
Lift 5.5 cm after yellow and visually refine the next placement toward the green bar center, using a smaller rightward move to avoid its edge.
Strike the center of the fourth, green bar with a vertical descent after the 5.5 cm lift from yellow. Keep the grasp closed.
Lift 5.5 cm after the central green-bar contact, then align above the fifth, light-blue bar while keeping the mallet clear.
Descend vertically onto the center of the fifth, light-blue bar after the clear lift from green. Keep the grasp closed and horizontal alignment fixed.
Lift 5.5 cm after the central light-blue strike, then move above the sixth, dark-blue bar while keeping the mallet clear and retained.
Descend vertically to strike the center of the sixth, dark-blue bar following the 5.5 cm lift. Keep the mallet retained and alignment fixed.
Lift 5.5 cm after the dark-blue-bar contact, then align above the seventh, purple bar while keeping the mallet clear and retained.
Strike the center of the seventh, purple bar with a vertical descent following the 5.5 cm lift. Keep the mallet retained and horizontal alignment fixed.
Lift 5.5 cm after the central purple-bar contact, then align above the eighth, magenta bar. Keep the left wrist left of center and the mallet clear.
Strike the center of the final magenta bar with a vertical descent, following the clear lift from purple. Keep the closed grasp and fixed horizontal alignment.
Lift vertically 7 cm after the final central magenta-bar contact, exceeding the required post-hit clearance, while retaining the mallet.
Return with the mallet well above the bars. Contact certainty remains limited, so prepare a carefully centered sequence with slightly deeper taps and clear lifts.
Complete the elevated return above the first red bar, keeping the retained mallet clear of every key and the arms separated.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged pose: recenter slightly left while elevated, then make a vertical red-bar tap. Right arm remains stationary.
Pause briefly at the red-bar tap, lift 6.5 cm vertically, then move one bar right above orange without sweeping at contact height.
Refine the elevated tip rightward to center it over orange, then descend vertically for the second tap. Maintain the closed grasp.
Briefly settle the orange tap, lift 6.5 cm clear, then move above the yellow bar for the next left-to-right strike.
